name: Worldpay
tagline: Global enterprise acquirer processing 55 billion transactions a year across 174 countries, now owned by Global Payments.
shortDescription: One of the largest merchant acquirers in the world, handling roughly 2.3 trillion dollars annually across 174 countries and 138 currencies. Pricing is a negotiated custom quote in the US; UK merchants get indicative calculator pricing with 24-hour settlement.
longDescription:
Worldpay traces its lineage to 1971 in Cincinnati, merged with the UK's Worldpay Group as Vantiv in 2018, and has changed hands twice since: FIS bought it in 2019, private equity firm GTCR took majority control in 2024, and Global Payments completed a 24.25 billion dollar acquisition of the whole business in January 2026. It processes over 55 billion transactions a year across 174 countries and 138 currencies, and sells everything from countertop card readers to full enterprise acquiring.

Pricing and how it works

Worldpay publishes no US rate card. American merchants negotiate a custom quote, typically interchange-plus for small business, and the monthly fees, PCI fees and any early termination fee all depend on the signed agreement. UK merchants get an indicative online quote instead: the calculator shows a per-transaction authorisation fee of 4.5p, a 20 pound monthly terminal rental, a 5 pound monthly PCI service fee, a 15 pound minimum monthly service charge and 20 pound chargebacks, with settlement in 24 hours. A UK pay-as-you-go ecommerce plan with no contract is also sold, reported by reviewers at 1.3% + 20p per consumer card transaction. US funding is fast: next-day is standard, with same-day funding and a push-to-card option that lands in about 30 minutes.

Who it is for

Worldpay fits established, higher-volume and multi-country businesses, platforms using its PayFac stack, and regulated verticals such as travel, gaming and crypto that many acquirers avoid. Micro-merchants who want transparent flat-rate pricing will find the negotiated contracts, monthly minimums and legacy terminal terms harder work than a Square or SumUp style provider, and the Global Payments takeover means products and branding are likely to keep shifting.

fees.inPersonCardRate: Custom quote, UK terminal plans from 20 GBP per month plus authorisation fees
fees.chargebackFee: GBP 20 in the UK, negotiated in the US
fees.pciFee: GBP 5 per month in the UK, varies by US contract
fees.monthlyMinimum: GBP 15 per month in the UK, varies by US contract
fees.earlyTerminationFee: None on UK pay-as-you-go ecommerce, applies to fixed-term agreements

pros: Scale few acquirers match: 55 billion transactions a year across 174 countries and 138 currencies
Fast US funding options, with next-day standard, same-day funding and a 30-minute push-to-card option
Takes on regulated verticals such as travel, gaming and crypto, and runs a PayFac stack for software platforms that embed payments
cons: No published US rate card, so rates, monthly fees and termination terms are all negotiated and hard to comparison-shop
Recurring complaints of fund holds, difficulty cancelling, mid-contract rate increases and long support hold times
UK terminal plans historically carried 18-month terms with exit fees, and monthly minimums plus PCI fees add up for micro-merchants

faqs.question: How much does Worldpay cost?
faqs.answer: Worldpay does not publish a US rate card: pricing is a negotiated custom quote, typically interchange-plus for small businesses. In the UK its online calculator shows indicative pricing of a 4.5p authorisation fee per transaction, a 20 pound monthly terminal rental, a 5 pound monthly PCI service fee, a 15 pound minimum monthly service charge and 20 pound chargeback fees. A UK pay-as-you-go ecommerce plan reported at 1.3% + 20p per consumer card transaction is available with no contract.

faqs.question: Who owns Worldpay now?
faqs.answer: Global Payments completed its acquisition of Worldpay on January 12, 2026 in a 24.25 billion dollar cash and stock deal, buying out FIS and private equity firm GTCR. Worldpay had previously been part of FIS from 2019 and majority-owned by GTCR from 2024. Expect continued product and branding migration under Global Payments.

faqs.question: How fast does Worldpay pay out?
faqs.answer: UK merchants settle in 24 hours on the indicative pricing plan. In the US, next-day funding is standard with a 7 PM Eastern cut-off, and merchants can opt into same-day funding or FastAccess push-to-card payouts that arrive in roughly 30 minutes.

faqs.question: Does Worldpay lock merchants into contracts?
faqs.answer: It depends on the product. The UK pay-as-you-go ecommerce plan has no contract and no exit fees, but UK terminal plans have historically run on 18-month terms, and US merchant agreements are negotiated and have carried early termination fees. Read the term sheet carefully before signing, especially for hardware bundles.
